headline: Drug tests failed
note: Paracetamol, BP pills and antibiotics among them.
source: CDSCO monthly drug alert, via The South First, 26 Sep 2026
coverHook: Paracetamol, BP pills, antibiotics: 220 samples failed India's own drug tests.
captionHeadline: 220 medicine batches failed India's own quality tests in a single month. Paracetamol, BP pills and antibiotics are on the list. Check your strip.
summary: In its August 2026 alert, India's drug regulator CDSCO listed 220 samples as "not of standard quality". They include batches of paracetamol, the BP drug telmisartan, antibiotics like amoxicillin and azithromycin, and injections. One batch labelled Telma AM was flagged as "purported to be spurious": the company named on the label says it never made it. Failures apply to specific batches, not whole brands.
forYou: Don't stop prescribed medicine. Buy from licensed chemists, keep the bill, check the batch number against CDSCO's monthly list, and report anything odd to your doctor.
cta: Jo ghar ki dawai laata hai, usse zaroor bhejo.

slides.label: THE LIST
slides.title: Common medicines with failed batches
points: Paracetamol: several batches failed the dissolution test
Telmisartan (BP): batches failed dissolution and assay tests

slides.label: FAKE, NOT JUST WEAK
slides.title: One batch may be a fake
slides.body: CDSCO flagged one Telma AM batch (18230791) as purportedly spurious. The company on the label told the regulator it never made it. The investigation is on.

slides.label: WHAT TO DO
slides.title: Protect your family without panic
points: Never stop a prescribed medicine on your own
Buy only from licensed chemists and keep the bill
Match batch numbers with CDSCO's monthly alert
Report side effects or odd packaging to your doctor

slides.label: SHARE THIS
slides.title: Your parents need this
slides.body: Send it to whoever buys the family's medicines.

collage.note: Check the batch number on your strip before you swallow.
